title: Z.ai Just Dropped GLM-5.4: A 'Loop Transformer' That Thinks Twice About Your Code!
summary: Z.ai released GLM-5.4 to GLM Coding Plan subscribers on November 23, 2026, introducing a Loop Transformer architecture that loops existing layers for deeper reasoning alongside native vision capabilities for coding, video, games, 3D shaders, and CAD. Weekly-quota subscribers receive 50% higher usage limits than GLM-5.3, while API access, open weights, and independent benchmarks remain pending.
raw_text: So check this out, because Z.ai just did something wild with GLM-5.4 for its coding subscribers! Instead of just throwing more parameters at the wall, they built what they're calling their First Loop Transformer architecture by actually looping existing layers inside the GLM-5 base model so it can do deeper reasoning. Here's the wild part: it doesn't just write software engineering code now—it brings native vision to visual coding and expands generation into video, games, 3D shaders, and even CAD modeling. Plus, if you're on a weekly quota, you're getting 50% higher usage limits than GLM-5.3 right out of the gate. Now, I gotta keep it real with you—unlike GLM-5.3, there are no open weights, API pricing, or independent benchmark tables dropped yet, and the rumored 1-million-token context window in Claude Code isn't officially confirmed in writing. Honestly, this is huge if the layer-looping magic holds up under real-world stress tests, so I'm definitely watching to see if Z.ai backs up the hype once safety checks wrap up.

title: Sarvam AI Open-Sources 105B Beast at Dirt-Cheap Prices—Is This the Flash-Lite Killer?
summary: Bengaluru-based Sarvam AI open-sourced Sarvam-105B-1711 on November 22, 2026, offering a 105-billion-parameter model optimized for reasoning, tool-calling, collaborative co-work workflows, and Indian languages. Co-founder Pratyush Kumar priced inference at 25 per million output tokens while publishing internal benchmark averages and training/inference recipes.
raw_text: So check this out, because Sarvam AI out of Bengaluru just open-sourced its upgraded Sarvam-105B-1711 model, and the pricing and ambitions here are seriously eye-catching. We're looking at a 105-billion-parameter model tuned for reasoning, tool calling, collaborative co-work workflows, and Indian languages, coming in at a crazy-low 25 per million output tokens alongside training and inference recipes. Here's the wild part: internal numbers cited in coverage put it at a 73.9 average across eight conversational-agent benchmarks, right next to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and ahead of GPT-6 Luna. Co-founder Pratyush Kumar is making a big push for sovereign AI in India—pointing out how many trillions of tokens get imported daily and why local GPU infrastructure and data residency matter. Honestly, this is huge for developers who want open weights without getting crushed by hyperscaler API bills, though we still need independent third-party audits to verify those internal benchmark claims. Let me know in the comments if you're testing this locally!

title: Ant Group Open-Sources Massive 560B Medical AI—Why Benchmarks Tell Two Stories!
summary: Ant Group began open-sourcing its LingSante medical AI model family on November 22, 2026, releasing LingSante-3.1-air-VL (124B total parameters) and LingSante-3.1-flash (560B MoE with a 1M context window) alongside health tools for its 150-million-user Afu app. While internal evaluations and the InclusionMed consortium rank LingSante-3.1-flash highly, Artificial Analysis's external MLCR-AA harness scored it at 23.3% on long-context medical reasoning.
raw_text: So check this out, because Ant Group just open-sourced its LingSante medical AI family connected to Afu—an app serving 150 million users and nearly 20 million daily health consultations. They're dropping weights for LingSante-3.1-air-VL and a massive 560-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model called LingSante-3.1-flash with a 1-million-token context window, plus tools like LingSante-Pulse, MedGuard, and real-time video consultations via LingSante-Live. Here's the wild part: on InclusionMed and Ant's internal tests, LingSante-3.1-flash looks top-tier, yet an independent MLCR-AA evaluation scored it at just 23.3% on long-context medical reasoning. Honestly, this is huge for open healthcare AI, and it's a massive wake-up call for why we can't blindly trust vendor benchmarks when real clinical decisions are on the line. What do you think—would you ever trust an AI doctor with numbers that split?

title: Robots Doing 312 Tasks Zero-Shot?! X Square Robot Drops WALL-OSS-1.0!
summary: X Square Robot unveiled WALL-OSS-1.0 on November 23, 2026, a vision-language-action (VLA) foundation model designed to unify visual perception, language understanding, and physical motor execution alongside XR Harness and WALL-API-1.0. In vendor evaluations, the system achieved a 55.1% zero-shot success rate across 312 real-robot tasks, with open-source code and weights slated for release.
raw_text: So check this out, because physical AI just took another loud leap forward with X Square Robot unveiling WALL-OSS-1.0! It's a vision-language-action foundation model built to connect what a robot sees and hears directly to physical motor control, bundled with XR Harness and WALL-API-1.0, and they're promising open-source code and weights. Here's the wild part: X Square Robot claims a 55.1% zero-shot success rate across 312 real-robot tasks—covering unfamiliar objects, tool use, two-handed coordination, and multi-step manipulation without task-specific fine-tuning. Valued over $2.8 billion, the company wants WALL-OSS to become an open standard for embodied robotics. Honestly, this is huge if open weights drop soon and independent labs can reproduce those numbers outside of vendor tests. Are we getting closer to general-purpose home and factory robots actually pulling their weight?

title: An AI Designed a Whole New CPU Architecture From Scratch—4.59x Perf-Per-Watt?!
summary: Architect Labs drew broad coverage through November 23, 2026 for Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU architecture whose ISA, microarchitecture, RTL, formal verification (over 800,000 lines of Lean), and 7nm physical layout were generated by AI agents. Using interaction nets across a tiled mesh with local memories instead of traditional pipelines and coherent caches, a simulated 7nm quad showed 4.59x performance-per-watt against an unnamed dual-issue in-order core.
raw_text: So check this out, because Architect Labs is getting major attention for Frostbite, a CPU architecture where AI agents handled the whole stack from instruction set and RTL to formal Lean verification and 7nm physical layout. Instead of classic fetch-decode pipelines and big shared coherent caches, Frostbite runs programs as interaction nets across a tiled mesh with small local memories and three-rule work stealing. Here's the wild part: in pre-silicon 7nm simulations across 25 small test programs, a four-tile quad hit 4.59x the performance-per-watt of an unnamed dual-issue in-order core. Honestly, this is a fascinating engineering experiment—watching AI invent non-traditional hardware topologies is super cool—but we have to stay grounded since these are pre-silicon simulations, the baseline core isn't named for legal reasons, and SPEC or PARSEC benchmarks haven't been run yet. Let's see how real silicon behaves when it tapes out!

title: LTTS Launches SDVault.ai for Smart Cars While Clearing Up Cyber Rumors
summary: L&T Technology Services (LTTS) launched SDVault.ai on November 23, 2026, an AI-assisted toolchain spanning software-defined vehicle (SDV) development from requirements and coding to testing and release assurance, backed by 15 patent filings. Early pilots pointed to 30-40% added engineering capacity and faster ticket triage, while LTTS separately clarified that its corporate IT systems remained secure amid market rumors.
raw_text: So check this out, because L&T Technology Services just rolled out SDVault.ai, a toolchain built to streamline software-defined vehicle engineering all the way from requirements and coding to testing and release assurance. They've filed 15 patents around pairing generative AI analysis with deterministic checks and human sign-off inside customer-controlled setups. Honestly, this shows how serious automakers and engineering firms are getting about deterministic guardrails as cars become rolling software platforms. title: OpenAI's Chief Scientist Wants Scaling Pauses Based on Perplexity—Will Washington Bite?
summary: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed on November 22, 2026 that frontier AI labs adopt shared development ceilings halting scaling until interpretability and monitoring milestones are met, anchored in metrics such as perplexity. Coverage on November 23 highlighted political friction in Washington—noting President Donald Trump's opposition to broad AI limits alongside an incoming Democratic Congress—as well as enforcement challenges across closed and open-weight labs.
raw_text: So check this out, because OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki just dropped a major proposal asking frontier AI labs to agree on shared development ceilings. The idea is to pause scaling until researchers hit concrete interpretability and monitoring milestones, using technical yardsticks like perplexity—how well a model predicts the next token—alongside behavioral checks. Here's the wild part: this lands right in the middle of a political tug-of-war in Washington, where President Donald Trump has pushed back against broad AI restrictions while an incoming Democratic Congress could take a very different stance. Plus, even if big labs sign on, getting everyone—including global open-weight developers—to follow the same rules is no easy feat. Honestly, this is huge because it gets to the core debate over AI safety versus speed. Do you think voluntary industry limits actually work, or do they just slow down one group while others keep building?

raw_text: So check this out, because Meta AI Chief Alexandr Wang just made a bold call saying superintelligence is arriving—and telling the industry to rethink where we focus our engineering energy. raw_text: So check this out, because the November 23, 2026 arXiv batch is full of papers looking closely at where AI models actually break down.
